newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai premier to work on strengthing Burma ties.
newsitem.headline: Thai premier to work on strengthing Burma ties.

text.p: Thai prime minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's visit to Burma later this week will focus on bilateral issues aimed at strengthening relations between the neighbouring countries, government officials said on Wednesday.
Officials said Chavalit was not expected to make any major deals with Rangoon during his May 16-17 visit and will only sign an agreement on border crossings between the two nations.
Thailand's army commander-in-chief, general Chettha Tanajaro, said Chavalit would also raise the issue of the 700,000 illegal Burmese workers in Thailand.
"I proposed to the prime minister he give priority to the problem of illegal workers in Thailand," Chettha said. "This is an important issue which will affect our national security in the future."
One issue of contention between the two nations has been the flow of Burmese refugees into Thailand -- mostly due to clashes between Burmese troops and ethnic rebels near the border areas.

"The Burmese always say that they will take those people only after Thailand can prove that they are Burmese nationals. But how can we prove that since those people never have proper documents?" an official said.
There are an estimated 100,000 Burmese refugees living in sprawling camps near the border in western Thailand.
Chavalit, a general and former Thai army chief, said after becoming prime minister in November that he wanted to talk to Burma's military government about Rangoon's human rights situation.

The Thai premier, who has close ties to Burma's generals, said then that he wanted to tell leaders of the State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) the world had changed and it was time to change with it.
Chavalit was also likely to voice his support for Burma's entry into the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN), officials said.
His visit to Burma was postponed from earlier this month because the timing did not suit Rangoon.

The announcement of the postponement came shortly after the United States imposed economic sanctions on Burma in April, banning all new American investment in the country, in condemnation of what it said was Rangoon's poor human rights record and its repression of the democracy movement.
The United States is also lobbying ASEAN members to drop the plan to accept Burma as a full member later this year.
